# lean-pkg init

bootstrap an empty registry and its event log.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg init [--force] [common flags]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--force` | re-create only if the existing registry is empty |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `init` | bootstrap an empty registry file and its event log; refuses an existing registry unless `--force` and it holds no packages; the `registry-created` event records the registry file name and schema version (no host path), and `"forced": true` after `--force` | `[--force]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## Examples

Create the registry and its event log once, at the default location (~/.lean-pkg/registry, or $LEAN_PKG_REGISTRY).

```bash
lean-pkg init
```

Sample output:

```text
registry created: ~/.lean-pkg/registry/lean-packages.yaml (version 3); events: ~/.lean-pkg/registry/lean-package-events.jsonl
```

The same with the registry file named explicitly; the global --registry flag goes before the command.

```bash
lean-pkg --registry ~/.lean-pkg/registry/lean-packages.yaml init
```
